newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl confident EU will reach stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Kohl confident EU will reach stability pact.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Thursday he was confident the European Union would agree on a stability pact to ensure the future single currency enjoys long-term stability.

Speaking to parliament one day before the EU opens its summit in Dublin, Kohl said he wanted the planned economic and monetary union (EMU) to start on time in 1999 and to adhere to the strict convergence criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.

"I am confident that we will find a solution that will show all citizens the determination of the European Union to create a euro with long-term stability," Kohl said according to the text of his speech.
EMU should be created "at the planned time, and of course with strict adherence to the convergence criteria," he said.

Germany has run into criticism from its EU partners for insisting on a stability pact with automatic penalties for EMU members who overstep its strict budget constraints after the monetary union starts.
The text of the chancellor's speech made no mention of details of the stability pact.
